props.gloss_en: (entertained) with what does he compensate? -- say, with bread
[with bread] he is eating that day's own meal
rather, 'he compensates' means he compensates with kinds of delicacies (targima)
the baraita: if he compensated with kinds of delicacies, he has fulfilled his obligation
the steward: for one like me, used to eat only one meal a day -- may I eat one meal and be exempt?
R' Eliezer: every day you draw out several appetizers in your own honour, and now you would not draw out one appetizer in your Maker's honour?
the steward: I have two wives and two sukkot, in Tiberias and in Tzippori -- may I go from sukkah to sukkah and be exempt?
R' Eliezer: No! for I say: whoever goes out from sukkah to sukkah has negated the mitzva of the first
R' Eliezer: one does not go from sukkah to sukkah
R' Eliezer: and one does not make a sukkah on chol hamoed
the Sages: one may go from sukkah to sukkah
the Sages: and one may make a sukkah on chol hamoed
and they agree that if it fell, he rebuilds it on chol hamoed
R' Eliezer's reason: the verse 'the festival of Sukkot you shall make for yourself, seven days' (Devarim 16:13)
make a sukkah that is fit for seven [days]
and the Sages? this is what the Merciful One says: make a sukkah during the festival
a person does not fulfil his obligation on the first festival day with his fellow's lulav
as it is written 'and you shall take for yourselves on the first day...' (Vayikra 23:40) -- from your own
R' Eliezer: so a person does not fulfil his obligation with his fellow's sukkah
as it is written 'the festival of Sukkot you shall make for yourself' -- from your own
the Sages: although they said one does not fulfil with his fellow's lulav on the first day, he does fulfil with his fellow's sukkah
as it is written 'all the homeborn in Israel shall dwell in sukkot' (Vayikra 23:42) -- teaching that all Israel are fit to sit in one sukkah
[for the Sages, לך] is needed to exclude a stolen [sukkah]
but of a borrowed [sukkah] it is written 'all the homeborn'
[for R' Eliezer, כל האזרח] is needed for a convert who converted in between and a minor who came of age in between
and the Sages? since they said one may make a sukkah on chol hamoed, no verse is needed [for the convert and the minor]
the incident: R' Ilai went to greet R' Eliezer his teacher in Lod on the festival
R' Eliezer: Ilai, you are not among those who rest on the festival
R' Eliezer would say: I praise the lazy, who do not go out of their houses on the festival
as it is written 'and you shall rejoice, you and your household' (Devarim 14:26)
R' Yitzchak: whence that one is obligated to greet his teacher on the festival
as it is said: 'why are you going to him today? it is neither new moon nor Shabbat' (Melachim II 4:23)
by implication, on the new moon and Shabbat a person is obligated to greet his teacher
no difficulty: this one [R' Yitzchak's obligation] -- where he goes and returns the same day
that one [R' Eliezer's praise of staying home] -- where he goes and does not return the same day
the incident: R' Eliezer stayed in the Upper Galilee in the sukkah of Yochanan b. R' Ilai, in Caesarea (and some say in Caesarion)
the sun reached the sukkah; Yochanan: may I spread a sheet over it? (asked again at 27b.11 when the sun reached half the sukkah)
R' Eliezer: there is no tribe of Israel that did not produce a judge
R' Eliezer: there is no tribe of Israel from which prophets did not issue; the tribes of Judah and Benjamin set up kings by the word of prophets
the sun reached R' Eliezer's feet; Yochanan took a sheet and spread it over it
R' Eliezer slung his cloak behind him and went out
not because he put him off with words, but because he never said a thing he had not heard from his teacher
it was another festival
it was Shabbat
a window shutter -- R' Eliezer: when it is tied and hanging, one may shutter with it
R' Eliezer: and if not, one may not shutter with it
the Sages: either way one may shutter
(entertained) let him resolve [the sheet question] from his own ruling: the sheet is like the shutter that is not tied and hanging
there [the shutter] he nullifies it; but here, where he does not nullify it -- no
the incident: R' Eliezer stayed in the Upper Galilee and they asked him thirty halakhot of sukkah
to twelve he said 'I heard', to eighteen 'I did not hear'
R' Yosei b. R' Yehuda: the reverse -- to eighteen he said 'I heard', to twelve 'I did not hear'
they said to him: are all your words only from what you heard?
R' Eliezer: you have compelled me to say a thing I did not hear from my teachers
R' Eliezer: in my days no one preceded me into the study hall
and I never slept in the study hall, neither fixed sleep nor a nap
and I never left a person in the study hall and went out
and I never engaged in idle talk
and I never said a thing I had not heard from my teacher
they said of Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai: in his days he never engaged in idle talk
and he never walked four amot without Torah and without tefillin
and no one preceded him into the study hall
and he never slept in the study hall, neither fixed sleep nor a nap
and he never meditated [on Torah] in filthy alleyways
and he never left a person in the study hall and went out
and no one found him sitting silent, but sitting and studying
and no one opened the door for his students but he himself
and he never said a thing he had not heard from his teacher
and he never said 'the time has come to rise from the study hall', except on the eves of Pesach and of Yom Kippur
and so R' Eliezer his student conducted himself after him
Hillel the Elder had eighty students: thirty worthy that the Presence rest on them as on Moses, thirty that the sun stand still for them as for Joshua, twenty intermediate
the greatest of them all: Yonatan ben Uziel
the least of them all: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai

they said of Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai that he did not leave aside Bible and Mishnah, Gemara, halakhot and aggadot, the fine points of Torah and of the scribes, kal vachomer and gezera shava, calendar cycles and gematriot, the speech of ministering angels, of demons and of palms, launderers' and foxes' fables, a great matter and a small matter
a great matter: the Work of the Chariot
a small matter: the disputations of Abaye and Rava
to fulfil what is said: 'that I may cause those who love me to inherit substance, and fill their treasuries' (Mishlei 8:21)
they said of Yonatan ben Uziel: when he sat occupied in Torah, every bird that flew over him was burnt at once
